sections.text:
1 Leontium qui Zenone imperatore regnum affectavit et anno 483, ut videtur,
non Antiochiae sed Tarsi coronatus est, scimus ad seditionem movendam pro-
phetiis Pamprepii senatoris impulsum esse, quem μαγγανείας et τερατολογίας
insimulant christiani historiae scriptores (Theophan., p. 128, 10, 130, 3, ed. de
Boor; Damascius, Vita Isidori, § 110, ed. Westerman; Suidas s. v. Παμπρέπιος).
Cf. Rev. instr. publ., l. c., p. 10 s.
sections.en: 1 Leontius, who aspired to the kingdom under the emperor Zeno and in the year 483, as it seems, was crowned not at Antioch but at Tarsus, we know was driven to stir up sedition by the prophecies of the senator Pamprepius, whom of μαγγανείας ('sorcery') and τερατολογίας ('telling of marvels') the Christian writers of history accuse (Theophan., p. 128, 10, 130, 3, ed. de Boor; Damascius, Vita Isidori, § 110, ed. Westerman; Suidas s. v. Παμπρέπιος). Cf. Rev. instr. publ., l. c., p. 10 s.

summary.headline: Leontius’s Failed Coronation Chart
summary.text: Astrological discussion of planetary enclosures in inceptional charts, citing Dorotheus and Antigonus, followed by the chart and failed coronation of Leontius in Antioch, with planetary positions and an analysis blaming Mercury’s affliction by Saturn.
